title: Claims-Experience Loading on Rental Late-Renewal Premiums
content:
**Underwriting rule.** A Rental Property Service Contracts late-renewal premium carries a claims-experience loading that compares two amounts:

- **the benefit:** the benefit authorized on the contract in the twelve months before the late renewal, net of the authorizations reversed in those months;
- **the expired term's premium:** the expired term's annual premium charge plus every upgrade charge billed on the contract in those twelve months.

| Condition | Loading |
|---|---|
| the benefit is at least the expired term's premium AND the contract carries at least two benefit authorizations in those months | 0.12 |
| the benefit is at least half (0.5) of the expired term's premium but below it AND the contract carries at least one benefit authorization in those months | 0.06 |
| otherwise | 0 |

**Records read.** From the contract's claim records: the benefit authorizations and the authorization reversals, with their amounts and dates, in the 12 months before the late renewal. From its billing history: the expired term's annual premium charge and the upgrade charges billed in those 12 months.

**How the loading acts.** Every loading and credit on a late-renewal premium enters one adjustment rate — loadings added, credits subtracted — and the premium is multiplied once by one plus that rate, before rounding.

## Hypothetical contracts (expired annual premium $700.00, one upgrade charge of $60.00 in the 12 months, so the expired term's premium is $760.00)

| Net benefit in the 12 months | Authorizations in the 12 months | Loading |
|---|---|---|
| $800.00 | 2 | 0.12 |
| $800.00 | 1 | 0 (the first row needs two; the second row needs the benefit below $760.00) |
| $400.00 | 1 | 0.06 ($400.00 is at least $380.00 and below $760.00) |
| $379.99 | 3 | 0 |
| $760.00 | 2 | 0.12 |
